name: Bun
summary: An all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit combining a JavaScriptCore-powered runtime with a package manager, test runner, bundler, transpiler, and script runner.

features.name: Integrated runtime and developer toolkit
features.description: Bun ships a single executable that includes a runtime, package manager, test runner, bundler, script runner, and related TypeScript tooling rather than presenting these as unrelated command-line products.
benefits: Provides a consistent executable and workflow across development stages
Allows package, test, bundle, and execution operations to share platform code
costs: The executable and release surface spans multiple subsystems
Tool behavior is coupled to the runtime's compatibility and filesystem models

features.name: JavaScriptCore-powered runtime with source transpilation
features.description: Bun documents its runtime as powered by JavaScriptCore and able to execute TypeScript, JSX, and TSX by transpiling them before JavaScript execution. The fixed source contains separate runtime and JavaScriptCore integration components.
benefits: Executes common source formats without a separate user-invoked transpiler
Separates JavaScript execution from source-format lowering
costs: Transpilation adds source-compatibility and diagnostic behavior to runtime execution
JavaScriptCore-specific behavior remains part of the runtime contract

features.name: Event-loop and host API integration
features.description: The fixed Bun source contains an event_loop subsystem and runtime components for timers, networking, sockets, HTTP, and Node-compatible APIs, making asynchronous host operations part of the runtime implementation boundary.
benefits: Integrates asynchronous host operations with JavaScript execution
Provides web-standard and Node-oriented host APIs within one runtime
costs: Many host subsystems must coordinate scheduling and lifetime state
Compatibility behavior is broader than ECMAScript language execution alone

features.name: ESM, CommonJS, and package-manager compatibility
features.description: Bun recommends ECMAScript modules while supporting CommonJS, Node-style resolution, package scripts, workspaces, and a package manager intended for existing Node.js projects.
benefits: Bridges modern module syntax and the existing npm package ecosystem
Connects dependency installation, resolution, and execution workflows
costs: Multiple module and resolution conventions increase edge cases
Ongoing Node compatibility work creates a moving compatibility boundary

mathematical_views.question: How do runtime, package, test, bundling, and transpilation components compose around a shared executable boundary?
assumptions: Toolkit capabilities are vertices and shared source, filesystem, and process boundaries are edges
The graph describes architectural composition rather than implementation ownership
The view abstracts release packaging and platform-specific build details

mathematical_views.question: How does Bun transform TypeScript, JSX, or JavaScript source into JavaScriptCore-executed code?
assumptions: Source formats are input states and executable JavaScript is a later state
Transpilation and runtime dispatch are directed transitions
The model abstracts JavaScriptCore internals and source-map diagnostics

mathematical_views.question: How do ESM, CommonJS, Node-style resolution, and package-manager outputs determine executable module boundaries?
assumptions: Packages and modules are graph nodes with typed resolution edges
Installation and runtime resolution are related but distinct transitions
The graph does not claim complete Node compatibility or a fixed resolution order for every case

benefits: One executable spans common JavaScript workflows
costs: Broad subsystem coupling increases maintenance surface

benefits: Fast direct execution with built-in source-format support
costs: Transpiler and engine semantics are coupled to runtime behavior
Host API and scheduling state expand the runtime boundary

benefits: Practical interoperability with existing JavaScript packages
costs: Multiple compatibility modes increase resolution complexity
